units: Resistances are damage multipliers: 2 = takes double damage, 0.1 = takes 10%.

enemies.name: Alien Artillery Tower
enemies.description: An advanced alien defensive structure. It is specialized in long-range target neutralization and shoots highly explosive projectiles over a long distance. However, it is rooted in place, allowing the Mecha-Suit to outmaneuver the projectiles.

enemies.name: Alien Plasma Tower
enemies.description: This structure is an artificial construct of an alien species first encountered on Galatea 37. Alien technology utilizes dark matter and dark energy, which allows these structures to remain undetected in a hibernated state for a long time. Attacks its enemies by shooting powerful plasma projectiles.

enemies.name: Arachnoid
enemies.description: Arachnoids secrete strongly acidic substance from their tails and jaws. The acid is primarily used to make food easier to digest, but it can also be used offensively. Arachnoids are often seen attacking their enemies by launching acidic projectiles from their long tails. These projectiles are not thrown with great force making single projectiles easily avoidable.

enemies.name: Arachnoid Boss
enemies.description: Arachnoids secrete strongly acidic substance from their tails and jaws. The acid is primarily used to make food easier to digest, but it can also be used offensively. Arachnoids are often seen attacking their enemies by launching acidic projectiles from their long tails. These projectiles are not thrown with great force making single projectiles easily avoidable.

enemies.name: Arachnomortus
enemies.description: Arachnomortus is a formidable opponent, sporting a powerful and unique method of attack. By utilizing the innate properties of synthesized crystals, the Arachnomortus is able to launch razor-sharp crystal shards at its targets with incredible accuracy and speed.

enemies.name: Artigian
enemies.description: Artigian, a species of colossal pitcher plants, distinguishes itself by the imposing sack hanging beneath its 'mouth holes'. They form explosive balls of acids, which they then hurl at their intended targets. Upon impact, these volatile projectiles detonate, releasing corrosive substances that dissolve surrounding matter. Subsequently, Artigians utilize their extensive root networks, absorbing any liberated nutrients from the dissolved matter.

enemies.name: Baxmoth
enemies.description: Baxmoths have evolved their tall legs in order to reach the flowers high in the tree crowns. It's common for them to release a swarm of small, flying creatures, which behave like drones, gathering nectar for the Baxmoth and fending off attackers. It is unclear whether they are the same species, or if they live in a symbiotic relationship with each other.

enemies.name: Bio Factory
enemies.description: This alien structure replicates hybrid native-alien species of creatures found in the Metallic Valley biome, suggesting that those species do not reproduce on their own. If left undisturbed this structure will create an endless stream of hostile creatures.

enemies.name: Bitrid
enemies.description: Bitrid is a large insect that spends most of its adult life gathering nectar in its large sack, where it also keeps its eggs. Bitrids are hermaphroditic - any other member of the species can help with fertilizing the eggs. Once the larvae hatch from the eggs inside the sack, they feed on nectar until they're ready to emerge and burst the sack, killing the parent in the process.

enemies.name: Bomogan
enemies.description: A special set of organs on their backs allows these creatures to create sacks filled with easily combustible fluid. The sack is launched like an artillery shell and explodes upon impact. The explosive sacks can easily bypass defenses and hit critical targets inside the base. Thick bone plates on the front part of its body also protect the creature from all kinds of environmental hazards. Luckily, the creature is really massive and its small legs are not well-suited for chasing prey, so it is not difficult to outrun this behemoth.

enemies.name: Brabice
enemies.description: The Brabice is a floating creature that slowly levitates above the Cryo Fields. It observes its surroundings using a single large eye, tracking movement with quiet curiosity. Brabices are passive and appear more interested in observation than interaction.

enemies.name: Brabit
enemies.description: The Brabit species seems to be peaceful and neutral to other creatures. The mechanisms behind its ability to fly are not entirely clear, but readings suggest that it can manipulate the electromagnetic field around itself.

enemies.name: Bradron
enemies.description: This creature seems to be a result of a biomechanical experiment. Its natural organs have been cybernetically enhanced, allowing it to project a powerful laser beam from its prominent eye. However, their ability to hover above the ground seems to be of a natural origin, though it is currently unexplained. Could be related to the Brabit species.

enemies.name: Canceroth
enemies.description: The Canceroth, an enigmatic and formidable entity endemic to the Swamp biome, presents a multifaceted challenge to explorers. It features a central node surrounded by smaller cells, collectively wreaking havoc as they traverse the terrain without heed for obstacles. While targeting smaller cells can temporarily diminish their threat, the central node must ultimately be destroyed, a task complicated by the surrounding cells' protective function.

enemies.name: Canceroth – Nest
enemies.description: Constructed from densely packed organic material intertwined with fungal filaments, the Canceroth Nest provides a secure and nurturing environment for the development of Canceroth offspring. The surface of the nest is coated with a protective, mucous-like secretion. The nest's primary function is to support the growth and maturation of Canceroths.

enemies.name: Canomortus
enemies.description: Canomortus are small, crystal-infused creatures resembling Canoptrix. They can be summoned by Necrodons through unknown means, and their bodies are fused with crystalline growths. They exhibit similar territorial behavior, attacking any intruders with sharp claws and strong jaws. Despite their small size, their bodies are incredibly resilient due to the crystal infusion, making them difficult to defeat.

enemies.name: Canoptrix
enemies.description: Canoptrix are small, omnivorous creatures. They live in packs and it is very uncommon to see a singular specimen in the wild. They aggresively protect their territory, using their sharp claws and strong jaws to attack the intruder. These creatures can be found in moderate climate zones.

enemies.name: Canoptrix - Nest
enemies.description: This large organism seems to be a central figure in the Canoptrix reproductive cycle. The organism does not seem to belong to the same species as the regular Canoptrix, but the creatures always seem to lay eggs around it. It is suspected that due to the large and intimidating stature of this being the eggs are protected from predators.

enemies.name: Carnicinth
enemies.description: Carnicinths have evolved to disguise themselves as plants as far as even replicating their reproduction methods. Carnicinths are born from seeds and remain immobile for their entire lives due to their expansive roots. The roots do not serve any purpose when it comes to nutrition, as Carnicinths are carnivorous, but play a vital role in catching prey. Carnicinths have long tongues that they use to catch their victims. Being rooted deep in the ground ensures that the prey won't have enough strength to escape.

enemies.name: Cavernot
enemies.description: Gnerots feed on mineral deposits located all around Galatea 37 making them a common sight in every biome. It is unclear whether their bodies are covered in actual rock or if it is a product of their skin. This species seems to be able to manipulate the structure of Galatea's bedrock, causing large stony spikes to emerge from beneath the ground. Gnerots use this ability to attack targets out of their range.

enemies.name: Colgan
enemies.description: This creature lures unsuspecting prey with the vibrant colours of its back appendages. Once a suitable creature is close, Colgans quickly incapacitate it using their cryogenic saliva and razor-sharp spikes.

enemies.name: Crader
enemies.description: A small scavenger. It uses its sharp claws to rip whatever food it finds into smaller chunks that can fit in its mouth. Otherwise – this creature is harmless.

enemies.name: Crawlog
enemies.description: Crawlogs are a pack-dwelling species found in the caves and caverns of Galatea 37. Their pale, bony appearance and sharp claws make them formidable predators. Covered in glowing crystalline formations, they have adapted to the darkness of their environment, using their agility and speed to attack unsuspecting prey. Even more terrifying, they have the ability to return from the dead if not completely destroyed. Beware of their presence and be prepared for their relentless attacks.

enemies.name: Crysder
enemies.description: Crysders are small, peaceful creatures that inhabit the caves and crevices of Galatea 37. Resembling a hermit crab, they carry a glowing crystal on their backs. Crysders are known to scavenge for food and can often be seen feeding on mushrooms and other fungi growing within the caves. Despite their small size, they are quite quick and agile, making them difficult to catch or harm. As a result, they are often left alone by predators and other creatures that may pose a threat to them.

enemies.name: Crystaros
enemies.description: Crystaros is an impressive creature, adorned with an array of sharp, shimmering crystals protruding from its body. Its most noticeable feature is the two giant arms with towering, shield-like growth made of crystals on them. This species also feeds on crystals, and its diet seems to have influenced the structure of its body.

enemies.name: Crystug
enemies.description: Crystug is a slow-moving, snail-like creature that roams the caverns of Galatea 37. Its most striking feature is the giant, glowing crystal that protrudes from its back, providing both protection and a way to collect and store resources. Crystugs are known to collect and hide various resource shards that fall out of the shell upon their death, making them a valuable target for resource scavengers.

enemies.name: Darnot
enemies.description: The Darnot is a neutral flying creature, resembling an oversized and distinctly alien moth. Its iridescent wings span several meters, shimmering with an otherworldly glow that changes color in response to its environment. Unlike terrestrial moths, the Darnot's exoskeleton is adorned with bioluminescent patterns and intricate, spiny protrusions, giving it an eerie yet captivating appearance. With multifaceted eyes and elongated antennae, it navigates through the air with grace and precision.

enemies.name: Drexolian
enemies.description: Drexolians have a distinct ability to blend into their surroundings, disguising themselves as a regular tree. They are able to remain immobile for hours, only to strike an unsuspecting victim at an instant. They often try to immobilize their target with the use of their vine-like appendages.

enemies.name: Drillgor
enemies.description: Drillgor is a hulking behemoth that dominates the underground tunnels of Galatea 37. Its massive, razor-sharp claws are capable of tearing through solid rock, carving out tunnels that stretch for miles. Its appearance is nothing short of intimidating - with a carapace that resembles a crustacean and two curved horns that adorn its head. It moves with a terrifying speed and grace for a creature of its size, capable of covering huge distances in a matter of seconds. Drillgor is a force to be reckoned with in the dark and treacherous depths of the planet's caverns.

enemies.name: Fermentus Acidus (Acidic Yeast)
enemies.description: This interesting species of fungus is aggressively expansive. It multiplies heavily and resembles yeast on a much larger scale. The fungus takes control of as much space as it possibly can, spreading more eagerly towards sources of heat. The acidic by-products of its metabolism are released into the ground, significantly lowering the pH factor of the soil.

enemies.name: Flurian
enemies.description: Flurians seem to be biomechanically modified, however, no related organisms have been found on Galatea 37 so far. That might indicate that this species is entirely engineered. Highly territorial and aggressive, they attack intruders with their sharp claws and plasma projectile launchers fused with their arms.

enemies.name: Frigmon
enemies.description: The primordial ancestor to the Kermon species. Unlike Kermons, Frigmons do not possess a natural cloaking ability. However, they show more territorial behavior and are more likely to form large groups.

enemies.name: Frostiroth
enemies.description: This extremely resilient plant species can burrow even into the permafrost layer, thanks to the exothermal enzymes produced by its flower structure. The acid-like substance is also used for incapacitating prey.

enemies.name: Fungor
enemies.description: The Fungor is a colossal, towering creature that merges the characteristics of an animal with those of a fungus. It stands upright on six massive, gnarled tentacles, which propel its lumbering yet deliberate movements. Its body is enveloped in thick, spongy fungal growth, adorned with fungal spores. An additional, more agile tentacle extends from its back, swinging with deadly precision to attack its prey or defend against threats.

enemies.name: Geotrupex
enemies.description: These creatures are neutral scavengers and avoid direct contact with any other species. They spend most of their lives buried in the sands of Galatean desert. Thick carapace offers them some protection from physical attacks, often just enough to burrow underground and evade the attacker.

enemies.name: Glaciogan
enemies.description: Glaciogan's body is protected by thick plates of keratinous skin, resembling armor plates. Fat tissue accumulates beneath these plates and acting like an additional layer of insulation against physical threats and extreme cold.

enemies.name: Gnerot
enemies.description: Gnerots feed on mineral deposits located all around Galatea 37 making them a common sight in every biome. It is unclear whether their bodies are covered in actual rock or if it is a product of their skin. This species seems to be able to manipulate the structure of Galatea's bedrock, causing large stony spikes to emerge from beneath the ground. Gnerots use this ability to attack targets out of their range.

enemies.name: Gnerot Boss
enemies.description: Gnerots feed on mineral deposits located all around Galatea 37 making them a common sight in every biome. It is unclear whether their bodies are covered in actual rock or if it is a product of their skin. This species seems to be able to manipulate the structure of Galatea's bedrock, causing large stony spikes to emerge from beneath the ground. Gnerots use this ability to attack targets out of their range.

enemies.name: Granan
enemies.description: One of their most prominent features is the bioluminescent appendix on the top of Granans’ heads. It is used to lure small animals into the Granan’s giant maw. As if hundreds of teeth were not scary enough, these creatures can also spit acid, albeit at a short range. In case of shortage of fresh food, Granans will resort to scavenging.

enemies.name: Granan - Nest
enemies.description: Granans lay their eggs in this structure. It is similar to a honeycomb then it comes to its construction. Granan larvae hatch from eggs laid in the hive and remain there until maturity. The larvae feed on small insects lured to the hive by the bioluminescent appendages growing out of the structure.

enemies.name: Gulgor
enemies.description: Gulgors are dangerous reptiles found in the Crystal Caves biome of Galatea 37. Their bulky bodies and impressive claws make them formidable predators, but their real strength lies in their ranged attack, which involves releasing razor-sharp crystal shards from their puffed-up cheeks. Gulgors can also quickly burrow underground and ambush prey, making them difficult to track and avoid. Upon death, their bodies seem to be consumed by the earth, leaving behind crystal pillars as a haunting reminder of their presence.

enemies.name: Hammeroceros
enemies.description: These creatures are largely peaceful and do not attack unprovoked. They will try to scare off potential assailants by roaring and stomping their feet. If that has no effect, they will charge at the enemy head-first, using the entire mass of their bodies to their advantage. Large herds of these creatures roam the surface of Galatea 37, looking for optimal living conditions.

enemies.name: Hedroner
enemies.description: Hedroners can inhabit any liquid pool they find. They can even adapt to the extreme conditions of lava lakes. These creatures are rather reclusive and avoid close contact with other species. If Hedroners have to defend themselves, they rip out larcge chunks of the ground beneath them, which they throw at the enemy.

enemies.name: Hedroner Morphium
enemies.description: Hedroners can inhabit any liquid pool they find. They can even adapt to the extreme conditions of lava lakes. These creatures are rather reclusive and avoid close contact with other species. If Hedroners have to defend themselves, they rip out larcge chunks of the ground beneath them, which they throw at the enemy.

enemies.name: Hibernus
enemies.description: Instead of protecting itself from freezing, the Hibernus species deliberately allows thick ice layers to form over its body. Thick sheets of ice act like a natural insulator against the extreme weather, keeping the creature's core temperature stable.

enemies.name: Iceder
enemies.description: The Iceder is a small scavenger that feeds on organic remains left behind by other creatures. It shelters itself beneath a carefully sculpted ice crystal, using it as protective cover much like a hermit crab uses a shell. Iceders are cautious and rarely stray far from their frozen shelters.

enemies.name: Iceros
enemies.description: The Iceros is, on average, one of the largest creatures encountered on Galatea. Long tusks adorn its head and give the creature an additional tool in the fight for survival in its cold natural habitat.

enemies.name: Idapian
enemies.description: Idapians bear resemblance to another Galatean species – Vathamite. They seem to float in the air as though they were swimming in water. That suggests that their body density might be very low or that they affect the gravity field around them in a way that enables them to fly.

enemies.name: Idapian Metallic
enemies.description: This variant of the Idapian creature has been implanted with several synthetic elements, although presents no changes to behavior or bodily functions. Perhaps it was a failed experiment that was ground to a halt when it became clear that this species could not be weaponized.

enemies.name: Invigor
enemies.description: The Invigor is a predatory plant with a long, slender stem devoid of leaves or branches. Topping this stem is a large, heavy head bulb, crowned by a single antenna. Typically, the antenna is the only visible part of the Invigor, and it's the only part it wants you to see. When this antenna detects movement from suitable prey, the entire plant erupts from beneath the ground. The Invigor then uses its head bulb as a bludgeon, smashing its prey to pieces.

enemies.name: Jurvine
enemies.description: Jurvines do not create nests. They live a nomadic lifestyle, migrating from one feeding ground to another, not to overstay their welcome and become a target of a hungry Canoptrix pack. They move around on their very muscular legs, that they use to jump. This way they can cover long distances at a low energy expenditure. They move at very high speeds and are even able to outrun the Riftbreaker Mecha-Suit.

enemies.name: Kermon
enemies.description: Kermons live and hunt in small groups, targeting animals of all species as their prey. There is no direct evidence as of yet to confirm their ability to communicate with each other, but their cooperation and teamwork strongly suggest that. Kermons ambush creatures of all sizes and take them down with ease using their razor-sharp forearm blades. Kermons have the ability to cloak themselves in such a way that they become almost invisible to the naked eye.

enemies.name: Kermon Metallic
enemies.description: Kermons live and hunt in small groups, targeting animals of all species as their prey. There is no direct evidence as of yet to confirm their ability to communicate with each other, but their cooperation and teamwork strongly suggest that. Kermons ambush creatures of all sizes and take them down with ease using their razor-sharp forearm blades. Kermons have the ability to cloak themselves in such a way that they become almost invisible to the naked eye.

enemies.name: Krocoon
enemies.description: The Krocoon’s body looks as if it was made of metal or crystals. Such a strong body armor guarantees protection from most natural hazards, such as predators or weather events. The downside is that the creature is very heavy and is not the most agile. Krocoon is able to sustain itself by consuming raw minerals from various deposits on the surface of Galatea 37. In case of danger, it will use its hind leg or its head to crush the enemy.

enemies.name: Lesigian
enemies.description: These creatures have the unique ability to manipulate the electromagnetic field in their vicinity, giving them the ability to levitate, as well as cause lightning strikes.  These creatures are able to teleport from one place to another in order to throw the attacker off balance and gain the upper hand in combat. The mechanisms behind their teleportation technique are still unknown. Some Lesigians explode if their body is damaged, likely due to the electric charge stored within.

enemies.name: Lurkid
enemies.description: The Lurkid is a small, neutral organism endemic to the Fungal Swamp biome. Adaptable to both terrestrial and aquatic environments, the Lurkid thrives in the dense, moisture-laden habitat of the swamps. This creature's diet consists of microscopic flora and fauna, which it locates using its sensitive, antenna-like feelers.

enemies.name: Magmoth
enemies.description: Magmoths can be found within liquid pools of Galatea 37. All readings suggest that these creatures spend most of their lives submerged in the pool they're occupying. If they have to emerge above the surface, they shape the liquid around them to form an exoskeleton. It allows them to leave their home pool and relocate. Magmoths primarily rely on ranged attacks, shooting projectiles at their assailants.

enemies.name: Mantnice
enemies.description: The Mantnice is a peaceful flying creature native to the Cryo Fields, resembling a levitating stingray with a tail split into two trailing fins. It moves slowly through the air or hovers in place, carried by cold atmospheric currents. Mantnices are passive and spend most of their time drifting silently above the frozen terrain.

enemies.name: Moltug
enemies.description: Moltugs are large, slug-like creatures with a calcified shell on their backs. They feed on sulphuric residue found on rocks in the Magma Biome. For an unknown reason, Moltugs sometimes hide pieces of minerals underneath their shells.

enemies.name: Morirot
enemies.description: Morirots can only be found in the rocky Magma Biome. Their unusual habitat grants them invulnerability to heat and fire. They are protected by a thick outer shell, making them very dangerous foes. Morirots consume mushrooms both to get their nutrients, as well as water, which would be otherwise hard to come by. They usually live in large groups.

enemies.name: Morirot - Nest
enemies.description: Morirots seek out places like these to lay their eggs. The elevated platform is situated over an active volcanic vent, significantly increasing the surface temperature of the platform, but not to the point of killing the embryos inside the eggs. Once hatched, young Morirots hide in the small caves hidden at the base of the structure.

enemies.name: Mothray
enemies.description: Analysis of the Mothray's body composition suggests that it should be impossible for this creature to fly. Despite that, the creature is often seen calmly gliding across the Galatean sky, as if it was swimming. One possible explanation is that these creatures increase the density of the air around them, allowing them to 'swim' mid-air.

enemies.name: Mudroner
enemies.description: The Mudroner, a native species of the Galatean Swamp, often roams shallow waters in small packs. Taller and more slender than Hedroners, Mudroners feature elongated maws lined with sharp teeth and distinctive eyes emitting a purple glow to attract prey and warn threats. When threatened, they can sink into the ground and reappear elsewhere, continuing their assault from a safe distance.

enemies.name: Mushbit
enemies.description: Mushbits are often seen wandering between their hives. If left undisturbed, they will most likely ignore other species' presence, but if anything crosses their path they will attack ruthlessly. Mushbits are lightning-quick and their blade-shaped arms are sharp enough to cut through most metals. They live in large colonies. If you encounter one specimen, be on the lookout for more.

enemies.name: Mushbit - Nest
enemies.description: Mushbits create these structures as entry points to their giant colonies sprawling underneath the sands of Galatean desert. They are made from cellulose mixed with Mushbit saliva. Collapsing the structure permanently closes an entry point to the colony, significantly decreasing Mushbit presence in the area.

enemies.name: Necrodon
enemies.description: Extreme caution and further analysis advised. Necrodons might be just regular animals operating on instinct, but their behaviors suggest that they might be a higher level of species - more organized and intelligent than we thought.  It is unclear how, but they are able to bring fallen creatures back to life. In order to do that, the body of the creature must remain largely intact. Necrodons are not a big threat on their own, but become very dangerous in cooperation with other species.

enemies.name: Nerilian
enemies.description: Nerillians are able to burrow deep into the ground and remain there for days, waiting for prey to come by. Once they feel the vibrations of the ground caused by footsteps, they immediately rush to the surface to capture and kill their prey. They are very quick to attack and just as quick to burrow undergound if their target runs away or if it is too threatening for them.

enemies.name: Nurglax
enemies.description: Despite the horrifying appearance, Nurglaxes are not very dangerous on their own. They are slow and sluggish, which gives the Riftbreaker in a Mecha-Suit an advantage in direct combat. However, the sack growing out of the creature's back requires extreme caution. They are filled with Nurglax larvas and acidic fluid. These sacks are launched at the enemies. The acid corrodes all organic matter in the blast radius and the larvae gnaw at whatever is left behind.

enemies.name: Octabit
enemies.description: Very little organic matter can be found in this creature. It also does not seem to have any physiological needs – it does not eat or sleep. Reacts only to outside threats, as it chases the assailant and attempts to destroy it by exploding on impact. If attacked physically it will divide into smaller specimens.

enemies.name: Phirian
enemies.description: The creature uses its five muscular tails to push its tall, slender body along the ground. Phirians keep an upright position, giving them a great overview of their immediate surroundings. Despite being almost 10 meters tall, Phirian’s signature attack is a blisteringly quick dash towards the target, accompanied by a powerful thrust of the sword arm right through the victim. This is preceded by a short preparation period when the Phirian coils its body up in order to get the most strength out of its horrendously long and muscular body.

enemies.name: Plutrodon
enemies.description: The Plutrodon is a medium-sized, three-legged predator native to the Fungal Swamp, known for its speed and agility, using sharp claws to dig into the ground and climb surfaces like trees and rocks. Preferring to attack from a distance, it roots itself and summons pillars of spikes that damage everything in their path, making it particularly dangerous against fortified structures.

enemies.name: Poogret
enemies.description: The Poogret, with its endearing clumsiness and four spindly legs, presents a comical sight, further accentuated by its eyes protruding beyond its head, giving it a perpetually goofy expression. This creature sustains itself by consuming Garlimonium plants, processing them within its digestive system to produce nutrient-rich fecal lumps abundant in valuable resources.

enemies.name: Quelver
enemies.description: Their ovoid body is protected with an exoskeleton. The exoskeletal armor is enough to deter smaller predators, but larger ones will break it with no issue. Quelvers are scavengers. The creatures’ entire lives are centered around the search for organic remains they get their nutrients from. Despite the small size, these little bugs are quite fast thanks to hundreds of pairs of legs hidden beneath the body. If threatened, the Quelver will try to run from the danger as quickly as possible.

enemies.name: Rugwig
enemies.description: Rugwigs are scavengers, cleaning up all the organic remains they can find. They are harmless to the Riftbreaker and the base structures.

enemies.name: Shegret
enemies.description: Shegrets are usually not seen above the surface of Galatea 37. They spend most of their lives buried in the ground. These creatures are afraid of light and as such will only attack their target in complete darkness. Their long, sticky tongues allow them to extract any substance they need to survive, including pure energy. Shegrets display a preference towards inanimate objects, including Riftbreaker buildings. The lights of the Mecha-Suit are usually enough to scare them off.

enemies.name: Spawicer
enemies.description: The Spawicer is a crystalline nesting structure formed from dense cryo-organic material, used by various species of the Cryo Fields to lay and incubate their eggs. These structures serve as communal nurseries and are fiercely defended by nearby creatures. Some Spawicers exhibit unusual energy signatures, suggesting adaptive defensive properties similar to Omega-class organisms.

enemies.name: Spawrot
enemies.description: At the top of the Spawrot, the acid-spitting maw serves both a defensive and functional role. The maw periodically expels acidic substances to deter predators and potential threats, ensuring the safety of the nesting creatures within. This acidic secretion also contributes to the mound’s decomposition processes, breaking down organic matter to enrich the surrounding soil.

enemies.name: Spikodon
enemies.description: Using its sharp claws, the Spikodon species digs deep into the permafrost layer, building networks of underground tunnels that they use as their hives. It grants them protection from the extreme conditions of the Cryo Fields biome.

enemies.name: Stickrid
enemies.description: The Stickrid is a diminutive insectoid creature with an elongated body, utilizing six legs to hover above the surface of the water. Often observed in sizable swarms, Stickrids employ a hit-and-run strategy, launching acidic projectiles at their targets from a distance. Despite their numerous numbers, Stickrids are vulnerable to being crushed underfoot, making them a manageable threat when confronted directly.

enemies.name: Stonger
enemies.description: A very small creature that disguises itself as a rock. It seems to be a completely harmless scavenger that feeds off of leftover organic matter and mineral residue that naturally occurs in the Metallic Valley biome.

enemies.name: Stregaros
enemies.description: Stregaroses are covered by a thick carapace, making them very resilient to any forms of physical attacks. The characteristic structures growing out of their arms are made of the same tissue as the carapace. Stregaroses use these either as a shield or as a very capable weapon. Despite the size, the elements of their exoskeleton are quite light, allowing Stregaroses to move around freely.

enemies.name: Sulphorit
enemies.description: These creatures are peaceful, neutral herbivores, native to the Acid Biome. Their gastrointestinal tract is quite unique, as it doesn’t produce any acids on its own. Instead, they drink acidic sludge, which helps them digest their food.

enemies.name: Temperoth
enemies.description: Temperoth looks like an ice sculpture come to life. However, despite its appearance, it is not made of. Its body is covered with quartz crystals of various colours, which the creature can liquefy via an unknown mechanism. This allows the Temperoth to change shapes and quickly travel short distances as if it was swimming.

enemies.name: Vathamite
enemies.description: Bodies of Vathamites produce gases that are lighter than air as a byproduct of digestion cycle. Thanks to this, Vathamites can float in the air without wings. Their long, tentacle-like appendages catch small insects and pollen that these creatures feed on.

enemies.name: Venomine
enemies.description: They bear some resemblance to snakes, commonly found on Earth. However, they are not dangerous at all. They spend most of their lives looking for scraps of organic matter they could eat, as they are omnivorous.

enemies.name: Vesaurus
enemies.description: Like many creatures found on Galatea 37, the Vesaurus shows an affinity for mineral formations. They will often hover around the crystal formations, so often seen around the surface of the planet, and gather nutrients. In that regard, they are similar to hummingbirds but somehow the Vesauruses are able to remain airborne and stationary with only a couple of flaps of their massive wings, revealing massive differences in their body composition compared to their Earthly counterparts.

enemies.name: Viremoth
enemies.description: Viremoth is a truly enigmatic creature that can only be described as a sentient fog. It's hard to say whether it's organic or unnatural, as it seems out of this world. Viremoth can manipulate its shape and density, allowing it to move like a fog or condense into a more solid form. It can also generate electrical discharges making it a formidable opponent if provoked. However, Viremoth mostly keeps to itself, floating around aimlessly and observing its surroundings

enemies.name: Wingmite
enemies.description: A highly aggressive species, capable of traveling over long distances in a very short time, aided by the ability to fly over canyons and smaller rock formations. Once the swarm reaches the target they will try to shred it to pieces using their sharp claws. Appears to be a cybernetically modified version of another species, although no organic counterpart has been found.

enemies.name: Zorant
enemies.description: Zorants inhabit the desert areas of Galatea 37. Their four eyes give them excellent vision both during the day and in the darkness of the night. These creatures try to capture smaller prey by shooting electrically charged spikes out of the large gland situated on Zorant's back.
